subject.title: [Feature]:  Non-blocking heartbeat execution to prevent message processing delays

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a separate heartbeat execution lane or worker model, and what session-state and delivery-ordering contract should that model guarantee?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime scheduling, session ownership, and tool side-effect semantics, so automation should not choose the durable architecture alone.

options.title: Approve isolated heartbeat execution
options.body: Define a heartbeat-specific execution lane or worker contract with explicit session-state isolation, delivery ordering, retry, and tool side-effect rules before implementation.

options.title: Limit work to narrower mitigations
options.body: Keep heartbeat serialized and prioritize retry debounce, activity idle-timeout, session-lock, and TaskFlow recovery fixes instead of adding a new execution model now.

options.title: Keep current serialized model
options.body: Treat current busy-lane deferral plus lightContext, isolatedSession, timeoutSeconds, and skipWhenBusy as the supported model and close or narrow the broader request later by maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated heartbeat execution
recommendation.body: Define a heartbeat-specific execution lane or worker contract with explicit session-state isolation, delivery ordering, retry, and tool side-effect rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest heartbeat runner and retry history in the inspected commits and is the best routing candidate for the architecture decision.
